title: Differences in voice during different phases of the menstrual cycle
summary: This study aims to create a dataset that will enable the investigation of voice differences during various phases of the menstrual cycle. The focus is on whether predictive methods can be used to identify the phase of the cycle based on various speech parameters. The study includes speech recordings in three phases of the menstrual cycle (held vowels, read texts, free speech), which makes it possible to capture both vocal and content-related characteristics. After recording, various parameter sets are extracted and analysed using both classical statistical methods and machine learning techniques. In the long term, the findings could help to expand our understanding of hormonal influences on the voice and also offer potential for applications in areas such as health and communication.

interventions.name: Test subjects visit the laboratory at three points in their menstrual cycle (menstruation, ovulation, and late luteal phase) to make voice recordings.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
· Confirmed declaration of consent
· Minimum age of 18
· Native language German
· Regular menstrual cycle (between 22 and 36 days in the last 4 months)
Exclusion criteria:
· Use hormonal contraceptive methods
· May be pregnant
· Have perimenopausal symptoms
· Have received speech/voice training in the past
· Have had surgery on the speech system in the past
· Have consumed psychotropic substances (alcohol, drugs) shortly before the measurement
· Have acute illnesses or Covid-19 symptoms (e.g. fever, cough, shortness of breath)
· Have chronic respiratory diseases (e.g. COPD, ALS)
